key_insight: Concentrated attention-head dropout disrupts autoregressive reasoning more than diffuse dropout with the same masking budget.
engineering_relevance: Transformer fault-tolerance testing should assess clustered disruptions, not just average dropout rates.
method: Evaluate 250 paired GSM8K derivations per model on Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct.
Compare clustered attention-head masking with budget-matched diffuse dropout and stratified temporal redistribution.
Explore single-step dropout density versus multi-token continuity in a separate N=100 factorial analysis.
evidence_signal: At onset parameter B=0.10 (~5.7% scheduled vulnerable head-token volume), burst versus diffuse accuracy fell from 91.2% to 78.8% in Qwen (−12.4 pp; p=5.5×10⁻⁶) and from 84.0% to 76.8% in LLaMA (−7.2 pp; p=0.0198).
watch_item: Evidence is limited to two 8B models on GSM8K; the exploratory multi-token continuity effect was inconclusive.
paper_title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
